name: Bidi
summary: Isolates each Latin run inside Arabic copy, so sentence punctuation stays at the logical end of the line.
useWhen: Arabic copy with a Latin term in it: a product name, a file name, a format such as JSON, a URL
A sentence that ends right after a Latin word and shows its period on the wrong side
avoidWhen: English copy: it comes back unchanged, so the wrapper adds nothing
Copy with markup inside: Bidi takes plain text only
A whole paragraph in another language: give its element a lang attribute

insteadUse.A paragraph in English inside an Arabic: an element with lang en, or a Theme with lang en to change direction too

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: Each run is a bdi element with dir ltr. A run that opens with neutrals, like ~/.cursor, gets an explicit direction instead of a guess.
No invisible marks (RLM, LRM, U+202A to U+202E) are typed into strings: the markup sets the direction.

react.note: Lives in packages/react/src/theme/Bidi.tsx. The splitting is splitLatinRuns in @the-system/shared.

angular.note: A pipe or a component on splitLatinRuns from @the-system/shared.

native.note: Text runs with writingDirection from splitLatinRuns.

mistakes.wrong: Typing an LRM mark after a Latin word in an Arabic string
mistakes.right: <Bidi>{text}</Bidi>, which wraps the run in bdi

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the period in the isolate with the Latin word
mistakes.right: Let Bidi find the run: it never takes trailing punctuation

name: Button
summary: An action the person takes on this page: save, send, open, delete. The one control that renders a native button.
useWhen: An action that changes data or starts a task on this page
The main action of a form, a dialog or a card, as tone accent with emphasis solid
A secondary or quiet action next to the main one, as soft, outline or ghost
A link that must look like an action, through asChild
avoidWhen: A control with only an icon and no visible label
Navigation inside running text
A choice that stays on or off
More than one solid accent button in the same view

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density.

tone.description: The color family. accent is the primary action color of the active style.

emphasis.description: soft is the standard button of Studio and Desk (the source secondary). tone accent with emphasis solid is the primary action.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

loading.description: Shows the spinner and a visually hidden status (loadingLabel), sets aria-busy and data-loading, keeps the width and focus, blocks activation.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading, for example Saving changes or جار الحفظ.

disabled.description: Sets aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why. The native disabled attribute is never set. On an asChild link the href is removed while disabled.

start.description: Leading content: a system icon name or a node, before the label. Icons are 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

end.description: Trailing content: a system icon name or a node, after the label. 16px at every size.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of its container. Sets data-full-width.

wrap.description: Lets a long label wrap and the button grow in height. Off by default: the label ends in an ellipsis and the button shrinks with its row, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px. Sets data-wrap. Desk draws no roll on a wrapping label.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a link, as the button.

type.description: Native type, so a button never submits a form by accident. Ignored with asChild.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state, disabled and loading included. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; every solid fill gets the doubled ring (focus.shadow.primary) so it reads against the fill.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status inside the button says loadingLabel (Loading by default) and aria-busy is set.
notes: Disabled and loading use aria-disabled, not the native disabled attribute, so focus never drops to the page when an action starts.

While disabled or loading, a click or middle click does not submit a form or follow an asChild link, and onClick, onAuxClick, onPointerDown and onKeyDown do not run. A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.
Icons inside the button are hidden from assistive tech. The label names the button.
Under forced colors the focus outline uses Highlight and the Desk roll is off.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip (wave 1).

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Save changes, Delete project. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.busy: Keep the label while loading. Say the verb in progress (Saving changes) in a live region, not on the button.
en.danger: Name what goes: Delete project, not Delete.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حفظ التغييرات، حذف المشروع. Never the imperative.

react.note: Motion: press, named from the pattern catalog that arrives in wave 1. Today: instant color swaps, the spinner, and the Desk roll label.

angular.note: Host bindings set the same data attributes; Button.css is used as is.

native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android. No roll label.

styles.studio: Bordered and filled overlay pills. The primary action is the neutral fill from color.primary (overlay 20 with the control border); the accent tint is the overlay too. Hover and press step the overlay at once.
styles.desk: Pill shaped at every size. The primary action is yellow #ffd84d with ink text and a doubled focus ring; accent soft is a yellow tint. The label rolls up on hover and keyboard focus, a copy rolling in from below (recipes/Button.css), off under reduced motion and forced colors and on a wrapping label.
styles.neutral: Planned: filled primary, outline secondary, 36 to 40px.
styles.liquid: Planned: capsule buttons with a press scale.

mistakes.wrong: Two solid accent buttons side by side
mistakes.right: One solid accent button for the main action, soft or ghost for the rest

mistakes.wrong: A button labelled OK or Continue
mistakes.right: A verb plus a noun that names the result: Save changes

mistakes.wrong: Swapping the label to Saving while loading
mistakes.right: loading on the button and the busy verb in a live region; the width holds

mistakes.wrong: A disabled button with no reason
mistakes.right: Leave it out, or keep it focusable and explain with a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: An anchor styled with button classes
mistakes.right: Button with asChild around the anchor

mistakes.wrong: A Button with an icon and no visible text
mistakes.right: IconButton with a label

name: Field
summary: Wires one label, one description and one error message to one form control, and passes the invalid, disabled, read only and required state to it.
useWhen: Any form control that needs a visible label
A control with a hint that helps fill it, or an error that says how to fix the value
A settings row with the label at the start and the control at the end (orientation horizontal)
avoidWhen: A search box in a toolbar whose purpose is plain from an icon and an aria-label
A group of checkboxes or radios that shares one question
Read only text that is not a control

orientation.description: vertical: label above the control. horizontal: label at the start of the control's line.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. When not passed, the field is invalid while an error message shows. false hides the error.

readOnly.description: Passed to the control. Still focusable and readable.

required.description: Shows the required mark and sets aria-required on the control.

a11y.role: none on the root. The label is a native label bound to the control with for and id.
a11y.focus: The root is never focusable. Clicking the label focuses the control.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control. The field adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The description, then the error, are read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The error is not a live region and never role alert, so an error that is there when the page loads does not interrupt.
notes: The required mark is an asterisk glyph, so it does not rely on color, and it is aria-hidden. The control carries aria-required, not the native required attribute, so the browser shows no validation bubble.
The error starts with a danger icon, so it does not rely on color.
Controls read the wiring with useFieldControl(): id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly. A value the control passes itself wins.
A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first invalid control.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.

en.label: A noun in sentence case that names the value: Email, Board name. No colon, no question.
en.description: One sentence that helps fill the field or says where the value shows. Not a repeat of the label.
en.error: Says what to do, in plain words: Add the part after the @. Never only Invalid or Required.
en.placeholder: Never the label. An example value at most: For example, spring launch.
en.required: Mark required fields with * and say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

ar.label: اسم بصيغة المصدر أو الاسم، بدون تشكيل: البريد الإلكتروني، اسم اللوحة
ar.description: جملة وحدة توضح وش يكتب أو وين تظهر القيمة
ar.error: يقول وش يسوي عشان يصلحها: البريد ناقص، اكتبه كامل. مو بس غلط
ar.placeholder: ما يكون بديل عن العنوان. مثال على القيمة بس
ar.latin: النص اللاتيني داخل العربي يمر عبر Bidi
ar.required: سطر واحد فوق النموذج: الحقول اللي عليها * مطلوبة

styles.studio: Semibold label, muted description, danger text error with an icon

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder used as the label
mistakes.right: A FieldLabel above the control, and an example value in the placeholder at most

mistakes.wrong: An error that only says Invalid email
mistakes.right: An error that says how to fix it: Add the part after the @, for example name@example.com

mistakes.wrong: role alert on an inline error that is there when the page loads
mistakes.right: FieldError, read through aria-describedby when focus lands on the control

mistakes.wrong: A red asterisk as the only sign of a required field
mistakes.right: required on Field: an aria-hidden asterisk glyph plus aria-required on the control

mistakes.wrong: A label with an id written by hand and a control with a different id
mistakes.right: Field gives both ids. A control id of its own is picked up by the label.

name: Icon
summary: One system icon drawn from the icon set of the active style, sized by the size.icon tokens.
useWhen: A glyph next to a label in a control, a menu item or a status line
An icon only control, where the control carries the accessible name
A status glyph that a label beside it already explains
avoidWhen: An icon that is the only way to tell a meaning and has no label
A brand logo or an illustration
A glyph drawn from a file outside the system names

name.description: A system icon name. Directional names say forward and back.

size.description: 12, 16 and 24 px. The numbers are accepted too.

set.description: An icon set id, pixel or line. Overrides the set of the active style.

label.description: Gives the icon role img and this accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden.

a11y.role: img when label is set, otherwise hidden with aria-hidden
notes: Icons are decoration by default. The control around them carries the name.
Names in the mirror list flip in right to left layouts. Brand marks, clocks and media controls never flip.

angular.note: svg[dsIcon] is generated by packages/icons/build.ts and waits in generated-pending until Angular is installed.

native.note: react-native-svg Icon is generated by packages/icons/build.ts and waits in generated-pending until React Native is installed.

mistakes.wrong: An icon named chevron-right that points the wrong way in Arabic
mistakes.right: chevron-forward, which flips in right to left layouts

mistakes.wrong: An icon only button with the label on the icon
mistakes.right: An IconButton with its own label and a hidden icon

name: IconButton
summary: A square action button with only an icon. Its label is the accessible name and the text of its Tooltip.
useWhen: A toolbar, a header or a row where the icon is well known: close, more, settings
A repeated action in a list where a text label would crowd the row
A close control in a dialog, a panel or a toast
avoidWhen: The icon alone does not say what happens
The main action of a form or a dialog
A choice that stays on or off

insteadUse.The main action of a view: Button with tone accent and emphasis solid

icon.description: A system icon name or a node. Hidden from assistive tech. 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

label.description: The accessible name, set as aria-label. A verb plus a noun. Never the native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows it on hover arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.

size.description: A square of size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px. Never under 24 by 24.

emphasis.description: ghost, because icon buttons sit in toolbars and headers. No link: an icon only link reads as neither.

shape.description: pill is a circle, square takes radius.sm, default takes radius.control (a circle in Desk).

loading.description: The spinner replaces the icon, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel, aria-busy is set, activation is blocked, focus stays.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example an empty link, as the button.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; solid fills get the doubled ring.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label prop is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel and aria-busy is set.
notes: label is required by the type, so an icon button always has a name.
At least 24 by 24 CSS px at xs (WCAG 2.5.8). Use lg (44px) in touch layouts.
No native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows the label on hover and focus arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.
Directional icons (chevron-back, arrow-forward) mirror in right to left layouts.
A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Close panel, Open settings. Not the icon name.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: إغلاق اللوحة، فتح الإعدادات.

react.note: Motion: press, named from the pattern catalog that arrives in wave 1. Today: instant color swaps, the spinner, and the Desk roll label.

angular.note: Uses Button.css and IconButton.css as is.

native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android, accessibilityLabel from label.

styles.studio: Ghost by default, the control radius, the overlay steps on hover and press.
styles.desk: A circle by default (Desk controls are pills). The solid accent icon button is yellow with a doubled focus ring, accent soft a yellow tint. No roll: there is no label.

mistakes.wrong: An icon button with no label, or the label in a title attribute
mistakes.right: label set; the hint in a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: label="trash"
mistakes.right: label="Delete file"

mistakes.wrong: A 16px icon button in a dense row
mistakes.right: size xs, which keeps the 24px target

mistakes.wrong: A Button with only an icon child
mistakes.right: IconButton

name: Input
summary: A single line text input: a native input in a bordered box with optional start and end adornments.
useWhen: A short value typed on one line: a name, an email, a link, a number
A search box, with the search icon at the start
A value with a unit or a currency shown inside the box
avoidWhen: Text longer than one line
A choice from a known list
A date, a color or a file

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px at default density.

shape.description: default takes radius.control from the style, a pill in Studio and Desk. pill is always fully round.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Still focusable, selectable and readable. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

start.description: An icon name, a short text such as $, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

end.description: An icon name, a short text such as px, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the input.

a11y.role: textbox, from the native input (spinbutton for type number, searchbox for type search)
a11y.focus: The input is the only tab stop. Clicking anywhere in the box that is not interactive focuses the input. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, and on to the next control
keys.Home, End: Move the caret to the start or the end of the value
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: Change the value for type number
keys.Escape: Clears the value for type search, as the browser does

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label. The Field description and error through aria-describedby. aria-invalid and aria-required from the Field.
notes: No native title attribute. Use Tooltip for a hint, or the Field description.
dir auto is not set: the value follows the page direction, so a field does not jump sides while someone types a Latin word into Arabic. Pass dir auto yourself for free text in a mixed language form.
Email, url, tel and number values always run left to right, and stay on the reading side of the form. Their placeholder runs in the page direction.
A long value scrolls inside the box. It is never cut with an ellipsis.
Read only looks different from disabled: a dashed border and a quiet fill, full contrast text, and it stays focusable.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.
Disabled uses native disabled and draws with opacity.disabled, like every control.
A value being checked shows the loader icon in the end slot for now. A Spinner arrives in wave 1 and replaces it.

en.label: Always a visible Field label, a noun in sentence case. aria-label only for a toolbar search box.
en.placeholder: An example value at most: For example, spring launch. Never the label, never an instruction the person needs after typing.
en.adornment: A unit or a currency the value is in: px, USD. Never words the label needs. No icon that only decorates, such as a paper plane on an email field.

ar.label: عنوان ظاهر دايم، بصيغة الاسم وبدون تشكيل
ar.placeholder: مثال على القيمة بس، مو بديل عن العنوان
ar.latin: البريد والروابط والأرقام تنكتب من اليسار لليمين حتى داخل العربي

styles.studio: Bordered transparent pill, the control border, a soft inner glow and the 2px achromatic ring on focus
styles.desk: The same pill and glow, in Instrument Sans

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder as the only label
mistakes.right: A Field with a FieldLabel

mistakes.wrong: An input with a title attribute for the hint
mistakes.right: A FieldDescription, or a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: A disabled input to show a value that cannot change
mistakes.right: readOnly, which stays readable and focusable

mistakes.wrong: dir auto on every input in an Arabic form
mistakes.right: No dir: email, url, tel and number run left to right through the CSS

mistakes.wrong: type date or checkbox on Input
mistakes.right: The DatePicker or Checkbox component

name: Theme
summary: Stamps every runtime axis on its own element, resolves what is not passed from the nearest parent Theme, and gives the subtree its direction, icon set and style data.
useWhen: At the root of an app, once, so tokens, base CSS, direction and icons apply
Around a subtree that needs another scheme, style, density, language or direction
Around a demo or a preview that shows one combination of axes
avoidWhen: Changing one color or size in one place: use a component prop or a token
Setting dir or lang alone on an element: the tokens, Radix and the icons would not follow
Wrapping every component: one Theme per subtree that changes an axis is enough

style.description: The style pack id. Any custom id is accepted. At the root the default is studio; nested, the parent's.

scheme.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested. A scheme the style does not list falls back to its default.

density.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested.

glass.description: Read only by styles that use glass.

dir.description: Follows lang when lang is passed and dir is not. Otherwise the parent's, then from lang.

lang.description: A BCP 47 tag. The system ships en and ar.

css.description: Inline styles for the Theme element, as a React style object. style is taken by the style axis.

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: dir and lang on the element let screen readers pick the right voice and let CSS mirror the layout.
The Radix direction provider follows dir, so menus, sliders and arrow keys mirror in right to left.
Arabic text gets IBM Plex Sans Arabic, zero tracking, taller lines and small text one step up through base.css. Body text keeps its size.

en.lang: Set lang on the root Theme. A Latin island inside Arabic is any element with lang en; it gets the Latin type back.

ar.lang: Set lang ar on the root Theme. dir follows as rtl.

react.note: Exports Theme, useTheme, useOptionalPart, themeAttributes and resolveTheme from packages/react/src/theme.

angular.note: dsTheme directive with the same inputs.

native.note: ThemeProvider passes the resolved theme object through context, with the same axis names.

styles.studio: Black body, Inter Variable, default density
styles.desk: Black desk, Instrument Sans, default density, window and dialog controls and titlebar turned on

mistakes.wrong: <div dir="rtl" lang="ar"> around a screen
mistakes.right: <Theme lang="ar">, which also sets dir, the Radix direction and the Arabic type

mistakes.wrong: <Theme style={{ padding: 8 }}>
mistakes.right: <Theme css={{ padding: 8 }}>: style is the style axis

mistakes.wrong: Reading data-style from the DOM to pick a branch
mistakes.right: useTheme().style, or useOptionalPart for a part only one style shows

name: TitleBar
summary: The bar at the top of a window or a panel: window controls at the start, the title, then trailing actions.
useWhen: The header of a Window, or of a Dialog drawn as a window in Desk
A panel header that needs a title and a close button
avoidWhen: The header of a page
A toolbar of many tools with no title

title.description: The title. One line with an ellipsis.

titleId.description: id of the title, for aria-labelledby on the window or dialog.

actions.description: The end slot: IconButtons and small Buttons.

a11y.role: none: a plain container. The title is a heading (h2 by default).
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Focus goes to the controls and actions inside.

keys.Tab: Moves through the controls, then the actions

a11y.announce: The heading is read in document order. A window or dialog points aria-labelledby at titleId.
notes: The title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM.
In right to left layouts a bar with controls keeps them at the top left and centers the title, as macOS draws it. A bar without controls mirrors.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics. Latin file names go through Bidi.

native.note: Native screens use the platform navigation bar.

styles.studio: A plain header on the panel surface with a hairline under it (recipes/Window.css when inside a Window).
styles.desk: The titlebar material, a 3% white over the glass, no divider. The lights sit at the start.

mistakes.wrong: A title in a native title attribute to show the full text
mistakes.right: The full text stays in the title; a Tooltip shows it

mistakes.wrong: Mirroring the lights in Arabic
mistakes.right: The lights keep their place and order; only a bar without lights mirrors

name: Toast
summary: A short notice that something happened, shown in a corner and gone on its own. Called from anywhere with toast(); one Toaster renders them.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person took has finished: Draft saved, Link copied
A failure the person can fix later or retry from the toast, as tone danger with one action
A background event worth knowing now: a new version, a finished upload
Progress that ends in a result, updated in place with toast.update
avoidWhen: The person needs to make a decision before going on
Long content, a list, or anything to read twice
A critical error that blocks the task or loses data
A message tied to one field or one place on the page
Something that must stay on screen while the condition lasts

tone.description: The color and icon, and the timing: neutral, info and success close after 4s, warning after 6s, danger stays until closed.

title.description: One line: what happened, naming the thing.

description.description: More detail. Shown up to three lines; the announcement reads all of it.

duration.description: toast() option. Milliseconds before it closes; Infinity keeps it. Default by tone. Ignored for danger.

action.description: toast() option. One button: { label, onAction, altText }. altText is what a screen reader hears in its place, for example where else the same action lives.

dedupeKey.description: toast() option. A toast that reads the same as an open one bumps its count instead of stacking; a key groups repeats with other copy; false turns it off.

id.description: toast() option. A call with the id of an open toast updates it.

lang.description: toast() option. The language of the copy when it differs from the page. The root gets lang and dir.

count.description: Toast prop. The repeat count; the Toaster passes it from the store.

onClose.description: Toast prop. Renders the close button and is called by it. The Toaster always renders it.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar.

position.description: Toaster prop. end is the inline end: right in English, left in Arabic.

label.description: Toaster prop. The name of the region. {hotkey} in it is replaced by the hotkey.

hotkey.description: Toaster prop. The keys that move focus to the toasts.

store.description: Toaster prop. The store to render. Default the app wide store behind toast().

a11y.role: The Toaster is a region (named Notifications) holding a list; each toast is a list item. The announcement goes through a separate visually hidden role status region.
a11y.focus: Toasts never take focus on their own. F8 moves focus to the list; Tab moves through the toasts, newest first, and each toast's action and close button. Closing the focused toast puts focus on the list.

keys.F8: Moves focus to the notifications list
keys.Tab: Moves to the next toast, action or close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Escape: Closes the focused toast, or the newest one. Above an open dialog the first Escape closes the toast and the next one the dialog.

a11y.announce: Once per toast (WCAG 4.1.3), when it appears: the toast label and its text, through a status region that Radix removes after reading. danger is assertive (Radix type foreground), the rest polite (background). The toast itself has no live role, so it is never read twice. A repeat or an update is read once more. The action is read as its altText, the close button not at all.
notes: danger toasts stay until closed. The others pause while the pointer is over them, while focus is inside, and while the window is blurred or the tab hidden (WCAG 2.2.1).
Swipe toward the edge closes a toast; the close button is the button path for the same action (WCAG 2.5.7).
Above an open modal dialog the toasts stay visible (z.toast is above z.dialog), stay in the accessibility tree and can be reached with F8, Tab and the pointer.
At most three toasts show at once; the rest wait their turn, so a burst never covers the page.
No native title attribute anywhere.

en.title: Say what happened and name the thing: Draft saved, Could not upload photo.jpg. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.description: Optional. What it means or what to do next, in one or two short sentences.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Retry upload, Undo move, Open draft. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. One action at most.
en.danger: Name the failure and what is safe: Could not publish page. Your draft is safe.
en.repeats: Keep the copy the same for the same event, so repeats fold into one toast with a count.

ar.title: Say what happened and name the thing, in noun forms where you can: المسودة محفوظة، تعذر رفع الصورة. No diacritics.
ar.action: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إعادة الرفع، تراجع عن النقل. Never the imperative.
ar.digits: Western digits. Latin names in the copy go through Bidi when the toast is rendered by hand.
ar.lang: Pass lang: "ar" when the page is not Arabic, so the toast gets the Arabic type and direction.

react.note: Toaster renders the shared store from @the-system/shared; toast is re-exported from @the-system/react.

angular.behavior: the shared toast store with cdk:a11y LiveAnnouncer
angular.note: Reuses the store, its timers and Toast.css as is; reports pause and resume like the React Toaster.

native.note: The same store. Safe areas and reduce motion from the platform.

styles.studio: A flat surface card with a hairline border and a 2px edge in the tone color on the inline start side.
styles.desk: Glass notifications as on the desk: strong glass fill, window blur, window radius and the soft window shadow (recipes/Toast.css). Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned: a white card with a small shadow.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass capsule at the top center.

mistakes.wrong: A toast for an error that blocks the task, such as a lost session
mistakes.right: An AlertDialog that says what happened and how to go on

mistakes.wrong: A danger toast that closes itself after a few seconds
mistakes.right: danger stays until closed; the store ignores a duration for it

mistakes.wrong: A toast with two buttons, or an action labelled OK
mistakes.right: One action at most, a verb plus a noun: Retry upload

mistakes.wrong: The same toast stacked five times by a retry loop
mistakes.right: Same copy, one toast with a count. Dedupe is on by default.

mistakes.wrong: A second Toaster for Arabic copy
mistakes.right: One Toaster per page; pass lang: "ar" on the toast

mistakes.wrong: A toast as the only place a result lives
mistakes.right: Show the result on the page too; the toast only says it happened

mistakes.wrong: Mounting the Toaster inside a dialog or outside the root Theme
mistakes.right: Mount it once inside the root Theme, before any dialog can open

name: Window
summary: An app window over the page: a title bar, a body and an optional footer. It opens from a trigger, moves, zooms, minimizes and closes. Desk draws it as a glass window with traffic lights; Studio as a flat panel with a close button.
useWhen: A tool or a document the person works in next to the page: a board, a file browser, settings
Several views the person arranges side by side and brings to the front
Content that opens from a control and should grow out of it
avoidWhen: A decision that blocks the page until it is made
A short message with no work in it
A list of actions behind one control
Content that belongs in the page flow

kind.description: Sets data-kind. canvas: a large window with a margin of layer around it, no body padding. finder: wide, the layer edge around it. settings: centered, as tall as its content.

title.description: Names the window through aria-labelledby. One line with an ellipsis.

actions.description: IconButtons or small Buttons at the end of the title bar.

footer.description: The footer part, for the window's Buttons.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Closing plays window-close, then unmounts.

zoomed.description: Fills the layer. Sets data-zoomed and aria-pressed on the zoom light.

onZoomedChange.description: With it, or inside a WindowLayer, the zoom light works.

minimized.description: Plays window-minimize toward the dock, then hides the window. Sets data-minimized.

onMinimizedChange.description: With it the minimize light works. The app shows the way back (a dock) and sets minimized to false.

frame.description: { x, y, width, height } in px: x from the inline start edge of the layer, y from the top. null lets the kind place the window. Controlled with onFrameChange.

onFrameChange.description: Called on every move by key or pointer, with the clamped frame.

movable.description: Drag by the title bar and move with the arrow keys. Default true inside a WindowLayer or with a frame, false for a window placed by its parent.

origin.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect the window grows out of and closes back into. Focus returns to it on close.

dock.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect a minimized window falls into. Default the bottom center of the layer.

modal.description: aria-modal and a Tab loop inside the window. Off by default: windows sit next to the page.

a11y.role: dialog, named by the title (aria-labelledby) or aria-label. Not modal unless modal is set.
a11y.focus: Focus moves into the window (the window element, tabindex -1) when it opens after mount, or on mount when its origin has focus. On close and minimize focus returns to the origin, else to the element that had focus, but only when focus was in the window or lost. The window shows the 2px ring on keyboard focus.

keys.Escape: Closes the window. A control inside that handles Escape itself (a menu) prevents it first.
keys.ArrowUp: Moves the window up 16px, while focus is on the window or in its title bar
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves the window 16px to the left on screen, in both directions
keys.ArrowRight: Moves the window 16px to the right on screen, in both directions
keys.Tab: Moves through the lights or the close button, the title bar actions, the body and the footer. With modal, Tab stays inside the window.

a11y.announce: The title is the accessible name of the dialog. The lights and the close button carry their own labels.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7): arrow keys move the window. The frame is clamped so 160px of the window and its title bar stay inside the layer.
Arrow keys pressed in the body (a field, a list) never move the window.
Moving is off while the window is zoomed, and for a window placed by its parent with no frame.
A long title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM as the accessible name. A Tooltip on the title comes with Tooltip in wave 1.
Double click on the title bar zooms, as on the desktop. The zoom light is the same action for every input.
No native title attribute.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case: checkout-flow.board, Account settings.
en.labels: Close window, Minimize window, Zoom window. Name the window when several are open: Close notes.txt.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: إعدادات الحساب. Latin file names inside Arabic go through Bidi.
ar.labels: إغلاق النافذة، تصغير النافذة، تكبير النافذة.

angular.behavior: cdk:drag-drop for the title bar, cdk:a11y for focus, the shared window manager
angular.note: Window.css, TitleBar.css and WindowControls.css are used as is.

native.note: Phones and tablets have no free windows. A native app shows the same content as a full screen or a sheet; see Dialog and Drawer.

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius and shadow, no backdrop blur, a hairline under a plain title bar, and a close IconButton (part close) at the end of it. No lights. Open, close and minimize fade on duration.base; zoom has no motion.
styles.desk: A glass window: material glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow. The title bar starts with the traffic lights (optional part controls, and the close light is part close): lit while the window is active, idle dots when it is not, glyphs on hover and keyboard focus. The window grows out of its trigger, closes back into it, zooms with a FLIP and falls into the dock. The layer carries the desk grain. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.

mistakes.wrong: A window that only moves with a pointer
mistakes.right: Window moves with the arrow keys while focus is on it or its title bar

mistakes.wrong: A Window used for a decision that must be made first
mistakes.right: Dialog

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for transitionend before unmounting
mistakes.right: Window awaits the animation's finished promise; under reduced motion it is 0ms

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the lights in Studio with CSS
mistakes.right: The style turns the controls part on or off in style.json; Window renders the close IconButton when it is off

mistakes.wrong: A minimize light with no way back
mistakes.right: Pass onMinimizedChange and show the way back (a dock row); without it the light is disabled

name: WindowControls
summary: The traffic lights of a window: close, minimize and zoom. 12px lights with 24 by 24 px targets, each an IconButton with its own label.
useWhen: The controls slot of a TitleBar in a style that turns the window controls part on (Desk)
A window picture where the lights are shown but do nothing, with no handlers
avoidWhen: A panel in a style without lights (Studio)
Any control that is not close, minimize or zoom of a window

onClose.description: Without it the close light is disabled.

onMinimize.description: Without it the minimize light is disabled.

onZoom.description: Without it the zoom light is disabled.

active.description: data-state active: lit. inactive: idle dots until hover or keyboard focus.

a11y.role: group, named by label. Each light is a native button (IconButton).
a11y.focus: Each light with a handler is in the tab order with the 2px ring around its 24px target. A light with no handler is aria-disabled and out of the tab order (tabIndex -1): three tab stops that do nothing slow a keyboard down, and a screen reader still finds them, dimmed.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next light with a handler

a11y.announce: Each light is named by its label. The zoom light reports pressed while the window is zoomed.
notes: Never color alone: the glyphs (x, minus, arrows) show on hover and on keyboard focus of the group, and in forced colors always.
The lights do not mirror in right to left layouts. They keep the order close, minimize, zoom from the left, as macOS draws them and as the source does.
Targets are 24 by 24 px and touch, so light centers are 24px apart (WCAG 2.5.8).
No native title attribute.

en.labels: Close window, Minimize window, Zoom window. Name the window when several are open: Close notes.txt.

ar.labels: إغلاق النافذة، تصغير النافذة، تكبير النافذة.

native.note: Native apps have no window lights.

styles.studio: Not drawn inside a Window (the controls part is off). Standalone it draws the same lights.
styles.desk: The traffic lights at the start of every window title bar.

mistakes.wrong: Lights as bare buttons or spans with click handlers
mistakes.right: WindowControls: each light is an IconButton with a label

mistakes.wrong: A light that does nothing but stays in the tab order
mistakes.right: Leave out the handler: the light is disabled and skipped

mistakes.wrong: Telling the lights apart by color only
mistakes.right: The glyphs show on hover and focus
